subject: Request: tolerance annex for uptime/latency + supporting evidence
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@northbrookhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 16:12:04 -0700
Subject: SLA tolerance annex request (Northbrook procurement)

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo this week. Procurement asked me to formalize a request: we need a 'tolerance annex' to be attached to the MSA that clarifies uptime and latency commitments for production traffic, plus the evidence we can request during SOC/technical reviews. High level asks: 

- Monthly uptime target: 99.95% for the Dedicated tier, with a defined calculation for maintenance and force majeure exclusions.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 1s for API calls originating in us-east-1 (rolling 30d window).
- Maintenance windows: maximum 4 hours per quarter, scheduled with 72h notice; emergency maintenance excluded but should be rare and explained.
- Remedies: we prefer service credits rather than termination as the first remedy; details to be negotiated.
- Evidence requests: runbook excerpt for incident response, recent availability reports, and a redlineable annex for our legal team to attach to the SOW/order form.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a short annex and the operational evidence listed? If not fully, please call out which items you cannot provide and why. Procurement would like a response by end of next week (Jul 2).

Appreciate it —
Maya
Maya Singh
Procurement Manager, Northbrook Health
procurement@northbrookhealth.com

Attachment: Northbrook_SLA_Tolerance_Request_20270624.docx (requested annex template)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@northbrookhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:07:12 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA tolerance annex request (Northbrook procurement)

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear asks and the template. Short answer: we can provide an annex with defined uptime calculation and standard exclusions, and we can share an operational runbook excerpt and availability reports. A couple of items for alignment before we produce a redlineable draft:

- Target & measurement: our standard Dedicated commitment is 99.9% monthly uptime. 99.95% is above our standard for Dedicated without a pricing/commitment adjustment. We can propose a pathway to 99.95% (capacity reservation + on-call escalation SLA) — will need to reflect in order form pricing or an availability credit schedule.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 300ms is doable for many workloads but depends on model choice, sequence length, and traffic profile. We can include language that Redwood will maintain p95 latency < 300ms and p99 < 1s for the set of model families listed in the annex, subject to a performance verification step during onboarding.
- Maintenance: 4 hours/quarter scheduled with 72h notice is reasonable; we ask that the annex explicitly exclude rolling kernel/hypervisor updates that require brief preemptions (we'll call these routine host patch windows and count them separately).
- Remedies: we prefer a graded service-credit table; termination for uptime breaches is rarely accepted.

Looping in Marissa (solutions) to capture technical caveats and Karthik (legal) separately for redlines. Will produce a first-draft annex + operational excerpts by Jun 28.

Next steps: can you share any expected model families (e.g., text-gen-large, embeddings-only) and expected QPS and typical sequence lengths? That will help us scope the verification.

Best,
Markus
Markus Klein | Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
phone: +1 415-555-0143

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Tolerance_Annex_Draft_20270625.pdf (stub)

From: marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 07:35:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SLA tolerance annex request (internal technical notes)

Markus / Karthik — forwarding my tech notes for the annex. Key points to include in the draft annex and evidence bundle: 

- Verification step: a 7-day performance validation during onboarding where Northbrook will run a representative prompt set at target QPS; we will publish a verification report (p95/p99/median) and a brief CPU/GPU utilization snapshot.
- Model families: if they plan to use large-context text-gen models (>8k tokens) we recommend a separate latency appendix; p99 will likely be higher for long context results.
- Cache & prefix behavior: clarify that cached responses and prefix-KV hits are accounted for differently in cost and may have materially lower latency; annex should define whether cached responses are included/excluded from SLO measurements.
- Operational evidence: provide last 90 days of monthly availability numbers (aggregated), an anonymized incident timeline for Sev 2/3 in last 12 months, and an excerpt from our incident runbook (containment, communication windows, RCA cadence).

I've attached an excerpt from the runbook that is safe for sharing (no internal IP).

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Operational_Runbook_excerpt.txt (excerpt, redacted)

From: karthik.iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:51:22 -0700
Subject: RE: SLA tolerance annex request (legal redline prep)

Folks — drafting notes from Legal: 

- We'll produce a redlineable annex that mirrors the requested sections. For the 99.95% ask, I'll include two paths in the draft: (A) a standard 99.9% table with service-credit schedule, and (B) an elevated 99.95% clause that requires a capacity commitment (titled "Reserved Capacity Addendum") and a pricing delta. That keeps negotiation clean.
- Exclusions: include planned maintenance (with notice), scheduled host patch windows (as Marissa noted), third-party infra outages, and force majeure. We should quantify what counts as a maintenance event (start/end times, rolling vs baton).
- Evidence sharing: we can provide anonymized monthly availability reports and a redacted incident timeline. SOC2 documentation is provided under NDA only; link procurement to our security portal/process.

I attached a working PDF (draft annex) and will follow up with a tracked-change Word once we finalize internal edits.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Tolerance_Annex_Draft_20270628-track.pdf (legal draft, internal)

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@northbrookhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement-northbrook <procurement@northbrookhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA tolerance annex request (Northbrook procurement)

Hi Markus / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the detail. Procurement reviewed the note and the two-path approach looks reasonable. A couple clarifications from our side before we accept a draft: 

1) Evidence cadence: we need availability reports quarterly for the first 12 months post-onboarding (not just on request). Is that feasible?
2) Verification window: the 7-day verification is fine; we will plan to run our representative loads as part of the POC.
3) Pricing: can you provide a ballpark delta for the Reserved Capacity Addendum (the number is just for procurement scoping)?

If you can answer 1 & 3 quickly, we'll circulate the draft to legal and procurement internally. Looking forward to seeing the redline.

Best,
Maya
Maya Singh
Procurement Manager, Northbrook Health
